design_rules: The transceiver rail +5V_XCVR must only ever be fed through the Q1 P-FET high-side gate driven by the U6 3V3-good supervisor via Q2 (net PG_3V3). Never connect U3/U4 VCC (pin 20) directly to +5V_POE: the RP2354 fault-tolerant pads tolerate 5.5V only while IOVDD is at 3.3V (R-HW-020, R-HW-044).

Every safe-state bias resistor must reference +3V3 or GND, never a 5V rail: R_TE to GND (TE=L); R_DC, R_ATN, R_REN, R_IFC, R_SRQ, R_CFG to +3V3. TE/DC land on GPIO26/27 which are NOT fault-tolerant, so a 5V pull-up there is a defect. The single deliberate exception is R_PE to +5V_XCVR (SN75160B 3-state select).

The RP2354A GPIO map is load-bearing for the PIO state machines and must not be reshuffled: GPIO0-7 = DIO1-8 contiguous with DIO1 lowest (R-HW-060); GPIO8/9/10/11 = ATN/SRQ/REN/IFC; GPIO12/13/14/15 = EOI/DAV/NDAC/NRFD consecutive for one PIO SM (R-HW-061); GPIO16-21 = W5500 SPI MISO/CSn/SCK/MOSI/RST/INT; GPIO22 spare test pad; GPIO26 = TE; GPIO27 = DC; GPIO28 = CFG.

The In1.Cu ground plane and In2.Cu power plane must be cut away entirely beneath the PoE cable-side region: nets POE_TAP_A1/A2/B1/B2, POE_VIN_P, POE_VIN_N and the D_BR1/D_BR2 bridges sit on the primary side of the DP9900's isolation barrier at up to 57 V DC. A ground pour running under those nets bridges the isolation barrier and defeats the module's isolation. Keep a creepage gap per IEC 62368-1 for 57 V working voltage and route no plane, no via and no other net through that keep-out. POE_VIN_N is NOT ground.

Assembly is hand-built, so passives may go on B.Cu at no extra cost and the 3D-printed enclosure accommodates them. Front (F.Cu) carries everything tall or mechanical: J1, J2, J3, M1, U1-U6, Q1, Q2, D_BR1/2, X1, X2, L1, L2 and LED1 (LED must stay front and edge-visible). Back (B.Cu) carries the 0805 R/C passives. Place each decoupling capacitor on B.Cu directly beneath its IC's supply pin so the connection is a through-via rather than a trace - tightest supply loop and no front-side area cost. Board stays 62 x 68 mm: do NOT grow it backwards, because depth adds mass and lengthens the moment arm from the RJ45 cable to the GPIB connector. The mechanical load path is the 112-024-113R001's two M3 jackscrews on 46.8 mm centres, not the 24 signal contacts.
